study.citation: Winter S, Jung LS, Eckstein RL, Otte A, Donath TW, Kriechbaum M (2014) Control of the toxic plant Colchicum autumnale in semi-natural grasslands: effects of cutting treatments on demography and diversity. J Appl Ecol 51:524-533
study.product: none: cutting was applied to CONTROL a toxic plant, not to collect medicine
study.site: Six regions in Austria and Germany
study.notes: Randomised cutting plots, 2008-2011 mean matrices. COMPADRE labels the comparison plots 'Unmanipulated'; the paper describes them as cut in June (conventional management). The aim was to reduce a toxic weed, and the cut removes leaves, not the medicinal seeds or corms: use as evidence on the timing of leaf removal, not on medicinal collection.

design_caveat: Randomised harvest treatment with same-population control.
